A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CurvGAD work and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–F. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph anomaly detection results and ablations in Tables 1–3, plus runtime measurements in Appendix C.2, Figure 4, and Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and runtime results reported in Section 5 and Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The mixed-curvature encoder, curvature decoder, Ricci-flow pipeline, reconstruction and classification objectives, and signature-estimation algorithm are unchanged. The terminology correction in Section 4.1.1 does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten benchmark datasets in Table 6 and retain the additional Cornell, Chameleon, and Karate Club illustrations. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same 16 comparison methods appear in Table 1. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the runtime comparisons in Figure 4 and Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix E retain the same transductive supervised evaluation, dataset-specific splits, 40%/20%/40% fallback split, AUROC metric, model settings, and hyperparameter configurations.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same Euclidean-only, individual-pipeline, no-Ricci-flow, unsupervised, and manifold-signature ablations. The curvature illustrations and appendix computational-efficiency analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random splits per dataset and report means with 95% confidence intervals in Tables 1–3. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation results, runtimes, and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, both report Reddit AUROC of 70.42 ± 1.03 for CurvGAD in Table 1 and Reddit runtime of 585.22 milliseconds in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, Theorem C.1, complexity arguments, and decoder derivation in Appendices B–D are retained without revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about curvature-based anomalies, interpretable dual-pipeline detection, applicability across homophily regimes, and gains of up to 6.5% over comparison methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations, runtime findings, and heuristic-signature limitations are unchanged. Replacing 'heterogeneous and homogeneous' with 'heterophilic and homophilic' in Section 4.1.1 aligns that sentence with the scope already stated throughout v1, without introducing a new substantive applicability claim.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. This supplies new code-access information; hardware, implementation settings, preprocessing details, and hyperparameter documentation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix F's withheld self-citation. Replacing the preprint notice with ICML proceedings information is a publication-metadata edit.

P1.justification: Local edits add the abstract's code-access sentence, correct the graph terminology in Section 4.1.1, and update the publication notice. Section organization and the remaining scientific exposition are retained.

P2.justification: The first-page additions cause limited text reflow across pages 1–2. Figures and table structures are retained, but v2 introduces stray 'dat' text overlapping the Figure 4 caption on page 16.

improvement.justification: The added code-access pointer improves reproducibility guidance, and the corrected homophily terminology improves precision. These are limited gains because the scientific methods and evidence are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the linked code's usability. The small new Figure 4 caption overlap slightly harms presentation but does not outweigh those benefits.
